title: fix: soft token accepts any PIN when no keystore file exists (conformance)
description:
pkcs11test ReadOnlySessionTest.UserLoginWrongPIN confirms: C_Login with a wrong PIN succeeds on a fresh soft token (no keystore file exists). The code treats a missing keystore as 'fresh token, any PIN is ok'. pkcs11test opens a session, attempts login with PIN 'simply-wrong', and expects CKR_PIN_INCORRECT but gets CKR_OK.

PKCS#11 2.40 §11.16: C_Login must return CKR_PIN_INCORRECT for a wrong PIN. A token without a keystore is not a token that accepts any PIN — it is an uninitialized token.

Design question: wolfP11 currently allows C_Login to double as C_InitPIN (first login sets the PIN). This means there is no way to distinguish 'first use' from 'wrong PIN'. Options:
1. Require explicit C_InitToken/C_InitPIN to set the PIN before C_Login works (most spec-compliant).
2. Store a PIN verifier (HKDF-derived token, not the key-encrypting key) so wrong PINs can be rejected without attempting full keystore decrypt.
3. Accept the non-conformance and document it.

File as research: determine which option fits the wolfP11 design goal and implement it.
